ruling: R12: derived read-only from a raw E01 chain, sanitized, scanned, eye-reviewed; unobserved variants stay synthetic-only

codex-0.153.0-ws-run.jsonl.line_format: one JSON object per openai-responses stream in Open order: stream (Open-order number), source, exchange, message_index (WebSocket only), method/status/content_type when recorded, label, retained_segments, first/last (wall, mono_ns of the first segment's first and last segment's last observation), text (the retained bytes, sanitized, as UTF-8). Host chatgpt.com and path /backend-api/codex/responses are common to every stream and not repeated. Every WebSocket message had exactly one retained segment; the two upgrade-exchange bodies were empty (no segment).

derive.py.role: the derivation and scan; re-running it on the source chain reproduces the fixture byte for byte

source.harness: Codex CLI 0.153.0 (codex exec --json), native binary sha256 a29d9e86eef88cbbd69f97ce8c590b1d0a287c8f77424f5eef226b883d7eaa22, ChatGPT subscription auth
source.provider_format: OpenAI Responses over one WebSocket (GET upgrade, 101, permessage-deflate inflated by the T11 relay): each client text message is one response.create (message 0 is a warm-up with generate:false; later ones chain with previous_response_id and carry only new input items); the server answers each with a stream of event messages ending in response.completed. Codex also sends the vendor events codex.rate_limits, codex.response.metadata and responsesapi.websocket_timing.

sanitization: provider IDs (response, item, call, turn IDs and cache keys, including usage.attribution item keys) -> consistent placeholders <prefix>_phNNN (32 distinct), so previous_response_id chains and call_id pairs are preserved
client_metadata (installation, window, session and thread IDs, turn metadata) dropped
safety_identifier, reasoning encrypted_content, delta obfuscation padding, access_programs values -> fixed placeholders
tool schemas in tools/additional_tools -> type, name and '<omitted: N chars>' descriptions

developer and user context texts (base instructions, skills/apps/plugins/permissions instructions, plugin recommendations, environment context) -> '<omitted: context text, N chars>'; the E01 goal text (public, §4.1) is kept
codex.rate_limits, codex.response.metadata, responsesapi.websocket_timing -> their type member only (account plan, rate limits, headers, telemetry dropped)
recorder producer and connection IDs are not written; the test supplies documented placeholder IDs

kept unchanged: model, message and tool structure, statuses, provider timestamps, token usage, tool inputs and outputs, assistant texts, and the shared run path /Users/Shared/goalcup-m2-e01/<run> inside tool inputs (not personal data, as E01 judged for its committed excerpts)
